intent: A supporting sentence under a question that describes its QuestionnaireItem to assistive technology.
typical_uses: A hint under the question (pick one, select all that apply)

dont_use_when.situation: A supporting line under one choice rather than under the question

invariants.text:
It renders a `

` with an id (the caller's `id`, or a generated one) that the item's fieldset lists in its `aria-describedby`.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the validation message in QuestionnaireDescription
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use QuestionnaireError, which shows only while the item is invalid and is announced as an alert

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state (an empty state object for this part), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

good.title: A hint under the question
good.code:
<QuestionnaireItem name="signals" multiple>
  <QuestionnaireTitle>What should every update include?</QuestionnaireTitle>
  <QuestionnaireDescription>Select all that apply.</QuestionnaireDescription>
  <QuestionnaireChoices>{choices}</QuestionnaireChoices>
  <QuestionnaireError />
</QuestionnaireItem>

bad.title: A validation message written as a description
bad.why: The description is always shown and never announced as an alert; QuestionnaireError is the part that appears when validation fails.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<RenderState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state (an empty state object for this part), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.
